title: Court Allows 15-Day Detention of Four Suspects in Mbobu Case
desc: A Nairobi court has allowed detectives to hold four suspects for 15 days as investigations into lawyer Kyalo Mbobu’s 2025 killing continue.
content:
A Nairobi court has granted detectives 15 days to hold four suspects as investigations into the killing of lawyer Mathew Kyalo Mbobu continue.

The suspects appeared before the Milimani Chief Magistrate’s Court on Friday, September 25, after being arrested during an intelligence-led operation. The court granted investigators additional time to complete their inquiries.

The four are Julius Cheruiyot, Nicholas Naula Lemiso, Noah Kipkurui Langat and Kennedy Kipkemei. Two of them are police officers, while the other two are boda boda riders, according to reports from the court proceedings.

The Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) had initially sought permission to keep the suspects in custody for 30 days. Investigators told the court they required additional time to conduct forensic examinations, analyse digital evidence, carry out searches and pursue other leads connected to the killing.

Mbobu was shot dead on September 9, 2025, while driving along Magadi Road in Nairobi. The killing has remained under investigation for nearly a year.

Investigators have alleged different roles for the suspects. Cheruiyot is alleged to have been the gunman, while Lemiso and Langat are suspected of involvement in transporting or monitoring Mbobu before the shooting. The allegations remain subject to investigation and have not been determined by a court.

The investigation has also produced a significant forensic lead. Detectives recovered a Ceska pistol that had been issued to one of the suspects, and ballistic examination reportedly linked the firearm to the shooting. Police have also recovered a motorcycle and mobile phones as part of the investigation.

Detectives are pursuing additional people they believe may have been involved. The investigation has also drawn a reported connection to the killing of clinical psychologist Dr Victoria Mutiso in Upper Hill earlier in 2026, with police identifying Inspector Kenneth Sang as a person they are seeking in relation to the inquiry. Sang remains at large, according to The Standard.

The 15-day detention period gives investigators additional time to process the evidence and pursue outstanding leads before the suspects are brought back before the court for further directions.

For Nairobi residents, the case represents a significant development in an investigation into a high-profile killing that took place on one of the city's major roads.

The suspects remain suspects, and the court's detention order does not amount to a finding of guilt.
